I graded Riley's submission `s1` for quiz 0001. The grades are in `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | Riley chose "the model reads the calendar itself". The model only writes the tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | Riley answered 1, as if the model runs all three tools itself. The right answer is 4 model calls. |
| q5 | partial | Riley said the result goes back to the model but left out why the program does that. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Riley described the tool descriptions well. The added claim that the model remembers its choices across sessions on its own is wrong. |

**Summary:** Riley understands the shape of the loop and why it needs a stopping condition. The idea to fix is who does what: the model writes text, and the program runs the tools and provides any memory.

**Next step:** Riley should re-trace the laser-cutter request on paper, labelling each step "model writes" or "program runs". Then Riley should redo q2 and q4, and give both the "what" and the "why" on questions like q5.

I also added `learning-records/0003-model-writes-program-runs.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I did not grade `s2`, the second attempt from memory. Do you want me to grade it next, to see whether M4 and M3 are fixed?
